summary.headline: Modis Navnirman Q1 FY27 revenue rose 27.92% YoY to INR58.26 crore; PAT up 25.81% to INR8.54 crore, though EBITDA margin fell to about 20%.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew 27.92% YoY to INR58.26 crore and 13.15% QoQ, with EBITDA up 14.25% YoY to INR11.65 crore and PAT up 25.81% YoY to INR8.54 crore. Management attributed the margin squeeze to war-related material and labour cost spikes in April-May, which it said have since stabilised. The company added Khar (Rashmi Icon/redevelopment) to its Mumbai footprint, bringing the portfolio to 25 projects (six ongoing, 14 completed, five upcoming). Management gave no quantified FY27 project-addition target, only that two to three projects are likely in FY27.

segments.name: Mumbai redevelopment projects
segments.commentary: Six ongoing, 14 completed, five upcoming; 25 projects in total across Malad, Kandivali, Borivali, Dahisar, Goregaon, Khar. Revenue recognised on percentage-of-completion (Ind AS 115).

segments.name: Rashmi Square / Rashmi Signature
segments.commentary: Together about 60% of Q1 revenue per analyst's question, which management did not dispute. Square at 22 slabs and roughly 80% of inventory booked; Signature at 20th slab and roughly 50-70% booked (figures varied within the call).

guidance_outlook: Management expects two to three new redevelopment projects in FY27, with no guarantee given tender uncertainty.

Four pipeline projects with aggregate GDV above INR800 crore: Rashmi Paradise to start in Q1 FY27 (this quarter), Rashmi Gold and Shectal in Q3, Khar in Q4; Govind Dalvi on hold due to a government stay on a 500-metre area.
Management cited healthy margins of around 20-30% expected per project, and 19-20% margins on upcoming projects.
Square and Signature margins are slightly below underwriting due to war-time material purchases, but not expected to be majorly hit over a two to two-and-a-half year timeline.
Management has not yet set a leverage ceiling or capital-employed framework per project.
capex_capacity: Under construction: about 12.11 lakh sq ft; upcoming pipeline about 10.5 lakh sq ft (per analyst's question, not disputed).
Rashmi Square completed 22 slabs; Rashmi Signature 20th slab; Rashmi Delight 14th slab; Rashmi Manorath 13th slab; Rashmi Icon and Rashmi Avenue at plinth stage.
Rashmi Signature and Square expected to be handed over with occupancy certificate in Q3 FY27.
Asset-light redevelopment model: partners with societies rather than buying open-market land.
demand_pricing: Management said pricing trends are similar to before, with no significant volatility; pricing is micro-market and project specific.
Management views Mumbai demand as stable with no decline expected over the next few years, though supply has risen due to government moves on MHADA and SRA land.
Demand exists for both luxury and affordable segments; product positioning varies by micro-market (larger homes in Kandivali/Borivali).
Labour availability and cost were described as not an issue at any project now, after war-time shortages in April-May.
Expansion limited to Bombay; Parle in tender, Ghatkopar under discussion, nothing finalised. Other Indian cities open in principle.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall from about 22.3% to about 19.8% despite 28% revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the hit mainly to the war, which raised material and labour costs and caused panic buying and shortages; it said costs have stabilised and Q1 is expected to track the company's stated margin levels going forward.

qa_highlights.question: How many new projects in FY27 and what is the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: No guaranteed count; two to three development stages where the company is in the top three bidders, plus further tenders. Four pipeline projects with GDV above INR800 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Are Square and Signature margins tracking underwriting?
qa_highlights.answer: Slightly below, because materials were procured during the war; management said the impact should be minor over the remaining two to two-and-a-half year timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory status of ongoing projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Square about 80% sold; Signature about 50% (later 63-70%); Delight about 40%; Manorath 20-25%; Avenue and Icon only recently launched.

qa_highlights.question: How will capital employed and leverage be managed?
qa_highlights.answer: No leverage ceiling or capital-per-project framework set yet, as each project has different economics.

risks_watch: Margin recovery: Q1 EBITDA margin compression from war-related costs; watch whether Q2 margins return to the 20-30% range management cited.
Pipeline conversion: tenders are uncertain; Govind Dalvi is on hold due to a government stay on a 500-metre area.
Supply increase in Mumbai from MHADA and SRA land releases could pressure pricing or absorption.
Working capital and leverage: no framework yet for capital per project or leverage ceiling as project size rises.
Sales velocity: Manorath at 20-25% sold and Icon/Avenue only just launched; Square and Signature inventory is largely booked.
Thin stock liquidity noted by an analyst; management attributed it to market conditions.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and execution, with a clear focus on delivery timelines. Evasive or non-committal on pipeline count, leverage and capital planning, which management said have not been set. Acknowledged war-related margin pressure as a one-off that has eased.
key_quotes: Because war situation happened, the cost of materials and everything increased.
But a healthy margins of around 20% to 30% should be expected in every project.
The projects are starting from now.
